result.title: The Predictive--Optimization Gap in GuanDan Self-Play
result.summary: Outcome-predictive signals are often treated as promising optimization targets in reinforcement learning, but predictive validity and optimization utility are different claims. We expose this distinction in GuanDan, a multi-round imperfect-information game in which the implication of a round outcome depends on the public match state. Held-out analysis shows that state--gain interactions provide incremental predictive value beyond a constant signed-gain effect, establishing that match progress is predictively meaningful. We then use changes in a frozen match-win predictor, $ΔΦ$, as a controlled round-level supervision intervention in a matched DanZero-style Monte Carlo self-play protocol. The intervention can succeed in an individual lineage: a selected progress-augmented checkpoint substantially outperforms its matched Baseline on a locked evaluation. Yet the method-level result reverses this impression: none of five preregistered replication seeds is positive, the pooled ten-seed interval includes zero, and across-iteration effects repeatedly change sign without a common late-stage advantage. These results identify a predictive--optimization gap: under the studied learner, a signal can describe outcome-relevant progress while failing to provide a reliably beneficial optimization direction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在贯蛋（GuanDan）多轮不完全信息博弈的自对弈中，以冻结的对局胜率预测器变化量 ΔΦ 作为轮级监督干预，先验证状态-增益交互具有增量预测价值，再通过多种子匹配实验发现该信号无法带来稳定优化收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽无视觉输入与 latent 状态生成，但其「预测有效性不等于优化效用」的论证及用冻结预测器信号作辅助监督并做预注册多种子复现的做法，可供核查 LVR 中进展/价值信号类训练监督是否真的改善推理状态，也提示贡献分配结论易被单条训练线偶然成功误导。
